turns.replyText:
Is a damaged item handled differently from a normal return?

Yes, a damaged item is handled differently from a normal return.

Here’s the basic breakdown:

Live plants (roses, perennials, bulbs)
We don’t accept standard “send it back” returns on live plants.
If something arrives damaged or you’re concerned about its condition, we treat that as a quality/damage review, not a normal return.
In those cases, our garden advisors review photos and order details and then decide next steps under our guarantee and warranty policies (which may include store credit if a claim is approved).
Non-plant items (tools, supports, markers, etc.)
Tools and other hard goods that are unused and just not what you wanted can usually be returned within our normal return window, and you’d mail them back in new, unopened condition.
Custom-engraved garden markers aren’t returnable unless there’s an issue with the engraving or a defect.
For damaged non-plant items, we still ask for photos and then the team decides whether it’s treated as a defect/damage issue or a standard return.

If you’d like, tell me what item is damaged (plant or non-plant), and I can walk you through the exact steps for your situation.

turns.replyText:
Will I get a replacement or a refund?

I’m glad you asked, because it works a little differently than a typical store return.

For damaged items, we don’t automatically send a replacement or issue a refund. Instead:

Our garden advisors review your photos and order details.
They decide what happens next based on our warranty and damage policies.
For live plants, approved warranty claims result in store credit, not a refund back to your original payment method or an automatic replacement. That credit can be used on our website.

To get this started so they can review your situation, please reply with:

Your full name
Your email address
Your order number
The name of the damaged item
Several clear photos of:
The damaged item up close
The whole plant/item
The shipping box and any visible box damage
